options.label: Human biology, disease and biomedical research
options.labelReason: The schedule follows the comparator's molecules-to-organism biomedical core, disease mechanisms, laboratory and quantitative research, translation and societal impact.
options.concept: Study how cells, genes and organs function in health and disease. Combine laboratory work and statistics with anatomy, infection, pharmacology and epidemiology to investigate mechanisms of disease and evidence for prevention.
progression: The life-science gateway precedes dependent biomedical study. Molecular Cell Biology and Life Science Laboratory precede pathology and disease. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics.

options.label: Molecular genetics, cancer and biomedical data
options.labelReason: Direct interests in molecular and cellular illness and genetics support a computationally stronger biomedical route centred on pathology, cancer-relevant disease mechanisms and research data.
options.concept: Study genetic variation, cellular mechanisms and disease, including cancer. Combine laboratory work with programming, data management, statistics, machine learning and image analysis to explore how computational methods can be used in biomedical research.
progression: Programming and mathematics precede advanced algorithms and deep learning. Introductory data handling precedes machine learning and deep learning. Molecular Cell Biology and Life Science Laboratory precede pathology.
options.distinctness: Six courses differ from the broad plan in each direction. This option adds programming, algorithms, databases, machine learning, deep learning and image analysis. It gives more weight to quantitative and computational methods than to anatomy, epidemiology and health psychology.

options.label: Human physiology, disease and mental health
options.labelReason: The biomedical core spans physiology, infection, disease and pharmacology. Developmental psychology, psychological assessment and psychotherapy give this option a distinct emphasis on mental health and illustrate diagnosis and intervention in that domain.
options.concept: Study human physiology, infection, disease and drug action alongside brain function and development. Examine psychological assessment and therapies to understand one way research informs diagnosis and treatment.
progression: The life-science and brain gateways precede dependent biomedical and behavioural courses. Laboratory and cell biology precede pathology and disease. Psychopathology precedes psychological assessment and therapies.
options.distinctness: Four courses differ from the broad plan in each direction. This option develops mental health and lifespan development through psychopathology, psychological assessment and therapies, and developmental psychology. Philosophy adds a complementary perspective on agency. The broad plan gives more weight to data, probability and evolution.

analysis: All three options have a substantial life-science foundation in biomolecules, gene expression, cell signalling, physiology, microbial and DNA laboratory methods, disease mechanisms, infection and pharmacology. Human physiology gives specific organ-system and homeostasis coverage. The broad option adds anatomy, epidemiological study design, health psychology and descriptive and inferential methods. Evolution replaces a broad hazards course in the broad and molecular plans, adding inheritance and genetic variation in populations. The molecular option replaces Psycholinguistics and hazards with evolution and algorithm design, and connects programming, statistics, databases, machine learning and neural networks. Databases contribute SQL, relational design and authorisation within the official description. Image processing supplies image filtering, segmentation and recognition with potential transfer to biomedical images. None of these technical courses alone reproduces sequence analysis or dedicated biomedical bioinformatics. The physiology option has substantive behavioural depth through psychopathology, clinical classification, interviews, psychological treatments and prenatal-to-late-life development. The philosophy course supplies a complementary account of agency and responsibility. It does not supply clinical practice. Perception & Action supports sensory and action mechanisms within the course description. The third option is better understood as human physiology and mental health than as a general translational-medicine programme. These plans differ by six, four and ten courses pairwise and concentrate different enquiry within a shared biomedical foundation. Utrecht’s integrated tumour project, specialised tissue study and assessed biomedical thesis are distinct from UCR’s distributed laboratory and research coursework.

candidateDecisions.label: Molecular genetics, cancer and biomedical data
Human physiology, disease and mental health

alignment.rationale: Both establish cellular and molecular foundations for human biomedical study.
Both study biomolecules, enzyme activity and metabolism.
Both study inheritance, variation and genetic information. UCR emphasises genetic testing and disease mechanisms.
UCR studies neoplasia and cancer mechanisms in pathology. Utrecht brings those questions together in a dedicated project on tumours and metastases.
Both integrate human physiology at organism and organ-system level.
UCR develops anatomy and structure–function reasoning. Utrecht studies differentiation and tissue types in greater depth.
Both study cellular signalling, membranes, gene regulation and cellular responses.
UCR studies population evidence and health interventions. Utrecht gives dedicated attention to collaboration among scientists, policymakers and the public.
UCR laboratory work supplies hands-on experimental practice within the comparator's broader compulsory methods component.
Utrecht requires supervised experimental work and a thesis. UCR teaches laboratory and evidence-review methods and offers optional independent research separately.
Both develop data analysis. Utrecht applies it to biological information, while UCR teaches general data handling and visualisation.
Students select a first-year biomedical elective from the official list.
Students complete at least four other courses from the restricted list in addition to Molecular Cell Biology.
The 45-EC profiling space remains open and is not treated as fixed comparator content.
